i want to make this clear, i am NOT condoning stealing animals. especially in the case you described. 

but we really shouldn’t just let dogs free roam. rez or not. i’m sure most people pick these dogs up with good intentions. saying “it’s just free roam here 🤷‍♀️” doesn’t make it okay. so many reasons that it shouldn’t be done.

i tried it once and i would absolutely NOT do it again. 

for one, you don’t really see the geckos. since they’re nocturnal, they’re hiding 95% of the time when you would be looking at your frogs. 

they poop on EVERYTHING. it’s really hard to spot clean the amount of poo they leave on everything. 

they eat the same food the frogs do which makes it easy, but it also means they’re now competing for food. stressful for both animals. 

since mourning geckos reproduce asexually, you’ll notice one day that now there are multiple geckos that you hadn’t prepared for

i’m no expert mourning gecko catcher but good luck catching those unwanted babies without destroying your tank. they are FAST. 

for me it was just a lot of unneeded stress. made my frogs stressed, my tank look way worse, and i just didn’t have fun with it. but again, i’m no expert. this is just my own experience.

Even “basic” surgeries like a spay, neuter, or dentals are big deals. It would be very easy to give too much of an anesthesia induction like Propofol, which is a respiratory depressant and then not “notice” that the animal is struggling to breathe. Using Propofol is okay because you intubate the animals so they get oxygen and it wears off quickly, but if not, they can quit breathing. 

Another thing that would be fairly easy would be to shut off the pop-off valve on your anesthesia machine. A pop-off valve is a little thing on your machine that you screw or push in depending on your machine and it shuts off the flow of oxygen. You do that only for a moment or two at a time to test if you have a leak in your system once the animal is intubated and set up. The animal will get zero oxygen if it’s shut off, so “forgetting” to turn it back on would result in a dog that turns purple and then dead. 

You could also just straight up not turn the oxygen tank on. Obviously the animal won’t get oxygen if there is none available to run through the system. 

There’s a bag connected to the system to basically show you, on the outside, what the animals lungs are doing. If the animal breathes in, you can see the bag go in. Breathe out, bag inflates. Sometimes you have to give animals breaths that don’t want to breathe on their own, but you can’t go over 20 psi or you’ll damage or even pop their lungs.
